provides: Public site content for a Stapel product: pages in a slug tree, a blog (posts, tags, date and tag archives, RSS/Atom), menus (header/footer trees targeting pages, posts, URLs or named frontend routes), SEO fields and a sitemap Function, and redirects written automatically when a published page or post moves. Bodies are typed block lists (rich_text as a ProseMirror/TipTap JSON document, hero, faq, gallery, embed with a host allowlist, a stapel-forms form by id, an opaque listing_rail query) validated by pydantic models from a MERGE registry, so a project adds its own block without forking. Staff write drafts, preview them by a signed link, publish now or on a schedule, keep editing while the published snapshot serves, restore revisions and archive; every publication is a fact. Content is site-scoped through the stapel-core site registry and locale-scoped with a fallback chain; a page can be copied into another locale, optionally through a machine-translation Function. The anonymous read is cached per site and answers conditional requests (ETag, Last-Modified). Not stapel-docs: docs is private workspace documents; cms is what an anonymous visitor reads at a URL of the site.

gates.behavior: true: the public posts/tags/archive/feed routes and the staff posts/tags routes are mounted, and paths under BLOG_PATH_PREFIX/ are reserved for posts; false: those routes are not mounted.

curated.summary: true (default): the site has a blog — posts, tags, monthly and tag archives, an RSS/Atom feed. false: pages, menus and redirects only. Values: true, false.

gates.behavior: staff: the staff API checks is_staff; model_perms: it also asks has_perm('cms.<view|add|change|delete>_<model>') for the model each route touches.

curated.summary: staff (default): every staff account may edit pages, posts and menus. model_perms: a staff account also needs the per-model permission its role grants (the @access mandate), e.g. to let marketing edit posts but not legal pages' menus. Values: staff, model_perms.

gates.behavior: Saving an embed block on another host is refused; every public resolve answer publishes the list as meta.embed_hosts so the renderer's client-side allowlist equals the server's.

curated.summary: The exact hosts an embed block may point at (https only). Default: YouTube (incl. nocookie), Vimeo, Google Maps. Replace the list to allow another provider.

extension_points.name: BLOCK_TYPES
extension_points.summary: Block types a page or post body may contain: {'<type>': 'dotted.path.PydanticModel' | None} merged over the built-ins (rich_text, hero, faq, gallery, embed, form, listing_rail); None removes a built-in. A project's own block is a pydantic model (stapel_cms.blocks.BlockData, extra='forbid'); its JSON schema reaches the staff editor through GET staff/block-types/.

extension_points.name: EMBED_HOSTS
extension_points.summary: Hosts an embed block may point at (exact host, https only). Replace the list to allow another provider.

extension_points.name: MACHINE_TRANSLATE
extension_points.summary: Name of a comm Function {texts, source, target} -> {texts} used when staff copy a page into another locale with machine_translate. Empty = off; unreachable or malformed answers are a 503, never an untranslated copy.

extension_points.name: MEDIA_REFS_FUNCTION
extension_points.summary: comm Function that tracks which media content uses (default cdn.refs_sync); empty disables. Best-effort after commit.

extension_points.name: STAPEL_CMS_PUBLIC_PRESENTER / STAPEL_CMS_STAFF_PRESENTER
extension_points.summary: Swap keys (STAPEL_SWAP) for the public and staff presenters, so a host changes what the API shows without forking a view.

extension_points.name: cms.page.published
extension_points.summary: A page snapshot went live (now or at its scheduled time): site, locale, path, revision, translation group. CDN purge, search indexing and sitemap pings subscribe.

extension_points.name: cms.post.published
extension_points.summary: A blog post went live: path, tags, the staff author id.

extension_points.name: cms.redirect.created
extension_points.summary: A published page or post moved (or staff added a redirect): old_path -> new_path.

extension_points.name: cms.sitemap_entries
extension_points.summary: Published, indexable pages and posts of a site with hreflang alternates, keyset-paged: what a sitemap aggregator asks.

surface.name: block_model
surface.intent: The pydantic model of one block type; KeyError when it is not registered.

surface.name: block_type_schemas
surface.intent: [{type, schema}] for every registered block type — what GET staff/block-types/ serves to the editor.

surface.name: get_block_types
surface.intent: The effective block registry (built-ins <- settings <- runtime). Ask it instead of reading the setting.

surface.name: iter_text
surface.intent: Every human-text string inside blocks (headings, labels, text nodes, alt), skipping URLs, media refs and opaque queries: the word count and the translation batch read this.

surface.name: map_text
surface.intent: A copy of blocks with every human-text string replaced by fn(text) — how a machine translation is applied without touching URLs or ids.

surface.name: media_refs
surface.intent: Every cdn media reference used inside blocks.

surface.name: register_block_type
surface.intent: Add a project's own block type (a pydantic model) from an AppConfig.ready(), or remove a built-in with None. The settings dict STAPEL_CMS['BLOCK_TYPES'] is the other door; both merge over the built-ins.

surface.name: reset_block_types
surface.intent: Drop runtime block registrations, leaving settings untouched — a test lever.

surface.name: validate_blocks
surface.intent: Validate a block list ({type, id, data}) and return its normalised JSON; raises BlockError with the error key. The staff API runs every save through it.

surface.name: word_count
surface.intent: Words in the human text of a block list (reading time).

requires.reason: comm bus (cms.* facts, sitemap/resolve/feed Functions, user.merged consumer), sitemap aggregator (cms registers as a provider when core ships it), site registry, AnchorPagination, GDPR owner protocol, @access, AppSettings
media references are cdn refs (<type>/<id>); cdn.refs_sync keeps pictures used by content from being swept as unclaimed; cdn.describe_many describes them in public answers (media, seo.og_image_url)
the form block embeds a stapel-forms form by its public_id
a content translation Function behind MACHINE_TRANSLATE copies a page into another locale machine-translated (upstream ask T1)
